text.p: Prices retreated on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Wednesday after rally attempts earlier in the week failed to stimulate a surge in copper.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index fell 1.83 points to 244.41.

Copper dipped to its lowest level for a week on Wednesday afternoon on the LME, but held above the strategic $1,900 level as speculators rushed to offer support, traders said. Selling pressure re-emerged during the kerb and prices ended $32 weaker at $1,913, but still inside the $1,900-$1,970 range.
Aluminium also ended off its low, lifting above its nadir of $1,335 in afternoon trading. Earlier speculative selling was met by solid support at the lows and the market finished at $1,342, down $14.
Many of the others ended weaker, but like aluminium and copper, bounced off their lowest prices.
Lead closed at $741, a loss of $9, but off its low of $737.
Nickel was nearly $100 down at one point, but ended with a $55 loss at $7,065.
Tin finished the late kerb weaker testing support at $5,950. The last trade was at $5,960, down $40.
Zinc was unperturbed by the gyrations of the others, holding to a narrow range and ending $1 up at $1,023.
Alloy ended the day at $1,225/28, down slightly from Tuesday's $1,230.

CBOT wheat closed lower on light exports with the market seeking direction after the late fund and local-related plunge in prices Tuesday, traders said. Traders said there was nothing to drive the market one way or another leaving the market vulnerable to further declines. Wheat closed three to eight cents per bushel lower, with December down 4-1/2 cents at $4.17-1/4.

Crude and oil product futures ended Wednesday's volatile NYMEX session lower across the board, with heating oil again leading the way. The market initially moved up after mildly bullish inventory data and November crude touched its post-Gulf War high of $25.70 a barrel. But profit-taking sent crude down almost $1.00 before it recovered to end at $25.14, off 28 cents on the day.

CSCE world sugar futures closed a dull session barely weaker, with prices consolidating amid dull trade, in the wake of Tuesday's volatile session, floor sources said. March finished 0.03 weaker at 10.70, having ranged from 10.77 to 10.67. The back months ended 0.01 to 0.03 lower.

New York precious metals futures ended mostly lower Wednesday, with the recovery of the past week now seen stalling, analysts said. COMEX December gold ended down 30 cents at $383.00, after falling back near the close from the session highs at $384.30. In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $380.90/381.40 an ounce, against the London Tuesday afternoon fix of $381.50, and the New York close Tuesday at $381.50/382.00.
